title: Git
subtitle: My governance platform reads git as evidence: witness, task and decision commits, authorship trailers, and the rule that every commit is pushed and nothing is rewritten.

stats.label: lines of Rust in the commit hook, tested against fake git clients

lede: AgentOS runs teams of coding agents that finish tasks constantly, often at the same moment, in the same repository. I wanted every finished task to leave a commit I could trace to its work order. I also wanted no agent touching git directly. So git became an output of the platform: agents never run raw git or push. When an agent finishes a task, a lifecycle hook commits the active work order's own project directory, and only that directory, as a tagged commit that names the work order and the task, so the history is searchable by the unit of work.
quote: Commits mark the work, carry attribution and stay out of agents' direct reach.
evidence: Version control as AI governance: tagged commits per finished task, decision and evidence, written by a lifecycle hook so agents never run git or push.
Concurrency control: commits scoped to one work order's directory under a shared file lock with a timeout, failing open with a report.
Rust systems engineering: a ~1,360-line commit hook tested against fake git clients, so every failure path is exercised without a real repository.
author: Corey James
